description: The World Container Index (WCI), assessed by Drewry Supply Chain Advisors, is a weekly composite of spot freight rates for 40-foot containers on eight major east-west trade lanes, used as an independent reference for index-linked contracts. The page read on 2026-09-29 gave the 24 September 2026 value: the composite fell 1% to 4,468 US dollars per 40-foot container because of lower Asia to Europe rates, while Shanghai to Los Angeles rose 2% to 7,838 dollars and Shanghai to New York stayed at 10,373 dollars. Each weekly update comes with charts and commentary on carriers' capacity management, and a Chinese version is posted on WeChat. Drewry states that its trackers and market indices are collected in a hub that needs registration and login but is free, and that coverage beyond the eight lanes is available on request. Coverage: eight main trade lanes. Format and access: web charts and commentary; free with registration. Licence and cost: free to view under Drewry's terms; no reuse licence is given. Caveats: spot rates only, with a proprietary method. It supports resilience and capacity planning studies of maritime supply chains, where rate spikes signal disruption. It complements the Freightos Baltic Index and UNCTADstat maritime statistics in the catalogue.
